sourceFacts: Double deadlift is the introduction before double swing.
Substantial single-bell swing, hand-change, clean and press preparation is discussed before paired-bell work.
Thumbs-back introductory swing, controlled trunk/standing and parking are emphasized.

appDecisions: Explicit experienced-trainee readiness and separate paired deadlift/swing confirmations.

Paired deadlift requires explicit hinge/deadlift technique and experienced-trainee readiness. Recent paired deadlift and single swing precede double swing. These configurable exposure windows are app recency gates, not a substitute for broader clean/press/hand-change experience.
Owned matched pair, explicit per-bell starting load, 2–4 sets of 5 with 90-second rest and conservative pace estimates.
Separate opt-in alternating foundation days and independent progression/load review. Existing double-clean/press/squat histories and admission gates are preserved.
Optional pairedSwingReps builds reps at two fixed sets, independently from the unchanged fixed-rep/add-set foundation profile. See paired-swing-reps-evidence.json.
limits: No compulsory source 6-to-20 cycle, fixed-year qualification, 60% load assignment or mandatory half-kilo increment. The numerical profile is explicitly selected and is an app adaptation.

Hand-to-hand and introductory single-arm swings now have separate tracked paths; neither their app evidence nor paired-swing rep progression certifies the broader single-bell preparation discussed by the source.
Outside swings, broader paired systems and physical/visual technique review remain incomplete.

doubleDeadlift.purpose: Practice controlled paired-kettlebell lifting as preparation for a familiar double swing.
setup: Review the paired-bell lesson and its substantial single-bell preparation context before beginning. A short app evidence window does not certify this experience.
Use a manageable familiar matched pair and a stable stance wide enough to clear both bells. Record load per bell; total external load is twice that amount.
steps: With both bells between the feet, hinge to take a controlled grip.
Stand fully with the trunk controlled, legs straight and glutes engaged.
Return the bells with a controlled hinge; practice the vertical lift before adding a ballistic swing.
bracing: Maintain abdominal and glute engagement rather than arching the lower back or shrugging the shoulders.
mistakes: Choosing the same per-bell load as a familiar single bell doubles total load; review a lighter familiar pair explicitly.
Dropping the bells or losing control on set-down: stop and revisit the controlled lift.
Treating two recent workouts as proof of paired-bell readiness: explicit experience and technique confirmation remain separate.

evidence.quote: we always work on the deadlift before we introduce the swing
set the bells down in the exact same position as you pick them up
most people need to go to lighter weights when they go to double bels

doubleSwing.purpose: Practice a controlled hip-driven swing with two familiar kettlebells after paired deadlift preparation.
setup: Establish substantial single-bell swing, hand-change, clean and press experience; review the source preparation context and confirm paired technique separately.
Choose a familiar matched pair, generally lighter per bell than single-bell work, with sufficient stance and swing clearance. Do not calculate a compulsory starting load from the source example.
Begin with both bells in front and a controlled hinge. Use the thumbs-back version taught for this introduction.
steps: Hike the bells back and drive through the hips to stand fully with grounded heels.
Keep the lats engaged and let hip drive move the bells; stop at or below shoulder height while retaining ribcage control.
Hinge on the return and park both bells under control in the starting position.
bracing: Keep the abdominal wall engaged, ribs controlled and glutes active at the top. The source demonstrates inhaling at the bottom and exhaling at the top.
mistakes: Thumbs-up sport technique is not the introductory variant taught here.
Bent knees at the top, backward arching or rib flare: reduce demand and revisit the standing/hinge pattern.
Straightening the legs to reach the floor during parking or dropping the bells: use the same controlled return as the start.
Automatic high-rep or heavy-pair jumps: the source describes long preparation and small equipment-dependent increments, not a universal starting dose.
